items.headline: Oil extends the slide in London — Brent ~$108.64 (-4.2%), WTI ~$99.71 (-4.2%) at 1020 GMT as Iran-Qatar talks enter a third day; OPEC+ held December output targets steady on Nov 1

Dollar softer in London — DXY fell to a 101.435 low (Fri close 101.879), EUR/USD up to 1.1237, GBP/USD to 1.3448, USD/JPY into the 157.60s as falling oil and lower yields (10Y into the 4.90s) weighed; Nasdaq futures rebounded just under 1% after Friday's tech rout
Japan's Katayama: no change in US-Japan FX coordination after the midterms; Tokyo will act on disorderly or excessively speculative moves; conditions improved since the yen's slide to 160
RBA tonight 9:30pm CT: Melbourne Institute expects a hike to 4.85% (fifth of 2026); ASX-futures model 70.8% for a rise; all four big banks expect a hike; published-research tally 10 hike / 2 hold

Oil slides ~3% in Asia as Doha talks enter a third day — front-month Brent ~$109.77 (-3.2%), WTI ~$100.53 (-3.4%); Tehran floats a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but tanker attacks keep the risk premium alive
Fitch cuts France's outlook to negative (Oct 30, unscheduled; A+ affirmed) — debt seen at ~124% of GDP by 2028, deficit 5.4% in 2026; euro languishes near a 17-month low at $1.1159 in early Asia

China RatingDog manufacturing PMI 52.0 in October — beats the 51.6 Reuters poll, in line with the 52.0 calendar forecast (prev 52.1); output growth fastest in six months but export-order growth slowed to a three-month low
Dollar rangebound into Tuesday's US midterms — DXY ~101.83 in Asia; the week's slate: RBA tonight 9:30pm CT, EZ flash CPI Wed 4:00am CT, BoE Thu 6:00am CT, US payrolls Fri 7:30am CT
RBA hike ~81% and BoE hike ~94.4% priced for this week (ActionForex Nov 2); JPMorgan joins the RBA hike camp, sees a tightening bias persisting
OPEC+ formally holds December output targets steady (Reuters Nov 1) — third straight hold at Sunday's online meeting; 2027 quotas due at the Nov 29 ministerial after a Q4 capacity review
